references.text: The description of how Bezalel actually built the incense altar out of acacia wood, fulfilling the instructions given in Exod 30:1.
The ark of the covenant was also made of acacia wood (עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים), the same material as the incense altar.
The bronze altar for burnt offerings was also made of acacia wood, another altar in the tabernacle with the same building material.
The priest was to smear blood on the horns of the incense altar (מִזְבַּח קְטֹרֶת) as part of the sin offering rituals.
Solomon overlaid the incense altar with gold in the temple, continuing the tradition of the tabernacle's incense altar.
King Uzziah was struck with leprosy because he unlawfully burned incense on the incense altar, which only priests were allowed to do.
Zechariah was serving at the incense altar (θυμιᾶσαι) in the temple when the angel Gabriel appeared to him.
The book of Hebrews mentions the golden incense altar (χρυσοῦν θυμιατήριον) as part of the tabernacle's furnishings.
John saw incense being offered on the golden altar before the throne, a heavenly parallel to the incense altar in the tabernacle.
Exod 37:25 shows the actual execution of the specific instruction given in Exod 30:1.
